title: Add compact onboard manifest and change serializer for delta release indexing
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Add deterministic change serializer to produce small delta bundles for release indexing
CLI hook to emit bundled changelog entries for releases
description:
Summary: Adds a compact onboard manifest (compact-manifest.v1) and a deterministic change serializer that emits compact delta bundles used by the release index generator and changelog automation.
Motivation: large model onboarding commits were producing verbose profiles and release artifacts; downstream release tooling and lightweight consumers (e.g., web UI, on-call tools, and offline auditors) need a concise, signed representation that is both verifiable and diff-friendly.
Design:
- compact-manifest.v1: trimmed metadata projection containing model identifier, canonical config hash, minimal performance profile pointers (tokenized perf tags), provenance fingerprints, and optional signature pointer. The manifest is JSONL-friendly and optimized for streaming over the onboard pipeline.
- change serializer: deterministic serializer that converts a set of model registry events (onboard, profile-update, variant-add) into a compact delta bundle. Each bundle is canonicalized (sorted keys, stable timestamps replaced with relative offsets) to make diffs small and reproducible.
- Signing hook: CLI/webhook that can attach an optional detached signature (ed25519) and a short provenance header used by the release indexer to validate release notes before publishing.
- Release indexer integration: the indexer now consumes compact manifests when present and aggregates succinct changelog blurb entries for release notes.
Checklist:
- [x] Define compact-manifest.v1 schema and compatibility rules
- [x] Implement serializer with stable canonicalization and tests
- [x] Add CLI emitter (redwood-registry onboard bundle --emit-compact)
- [x] Integrate indexer to prefer compact bundles when available
- [x] Add unit & integration tests for round-trip canonicalization
- [x] Add lightweight verifier utility used by the CI gating pipeline
Commits (summary):
- Add compact manifest schema and parser (a981f1c)
- Implement canonical change serializer and tests (b2d3e7a)
- CLI emitter for compact bundles and signature attachment (f7c4b1d)
- Indexer consumer changes + changelog blurb extractor (c33a19f)

Files changed (high level):

- registry/serializers/compact_serializer.py (new)

Testing and CI: Initial CI run surfaced two nondeterministic timestamp failures in the serializer unit tests; fixed by replacing absolute timestamps with monotonic offsets and adding a stable key sort pass. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint).
Review thread (condensed):
- Kai Patel (reviewer): "Nice reduction in payload size. Can we keep the full performance profile pointer for optional expanded views?"
- Author (Avery): "Yes — we keep an opaque profile pointer and a minimal tokenized perf tag list for quick routing. Expanded profiles remain in the registry for full diagnostics."
- Marta Alvarez (security): "Signature header format looks good; add a short nonce to mitigate replay when bundles are used outside the registry."
- Author: "Added nonce header and updated verifier to accept/validate nonce with a 7-day window as config option."
- Liam O'Connor (indexing): "Indexing changes LGTM; make sure consumer falls back to full profile for missing fields."
- Author: "Fallback path added; consumer logs a single warning metric when fallback occurs."
Edge cases and compatibility:
- If compact-manifest.v1 is not present, the indexer falls back to current behavior.
- Compact manifests are additive and fully optional; no registry schema migration required.
- Verifier is opt-in for now; CI gating can be toggled per-branch with the new registry-compact-gate pipeline.
Performance notes: The compact serializer reduces onboard artifact size by ~6x for large profiles in our internal tests; indexer latency for initial aggregation improved by ~30% in the benchmark lab (benchmarks included in test artifacts).
Security and audit: The detached signature and nonce allow offline verification by auditors; the verifier emits a signed verification provenance blob that the audit-log-exporter can ingest.
Backwards compatibility: Consumers that require the full profile still read the canonical profile from the registry using the profile pointer in the compact manifest.
Post-merge tasks:
- Publish docs/registry/compact-manifest.md (done as part of this PR)
- Announce the CLI flag in release notes and internal mailing list
- Add compact bundle generation to the model onboarding quickstart template (follow-up)
Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Kai and Marta; no additional changes required.
